**Page:** History – Davis Cup – The World Cup of Tennis  
**URL:** https://www.daviscup.com/en/about/history

**Evidence**  
- “Davis Cup began in **1900** as a competition between **United States** and **Great Britain**.”  
- “It’s now the world’s largest **annual international team competition in sport, with 157 nations entering in 2025**.”  
- **Honour Roll** (Nation – Number of titles)  
  - United States – 32  
  - Australia – 28  
  - France – 10  
  - Great Britain – 10  
  - Sweden – 7  
  - Spain – 6  
  - Italy – 4  
  - Czechia/Germany/Russia – 3 (split)  
  - Croatia – 2  
  - Argentina/Canada/Serbia/South Africa/Switzerland – 1 each  
- **Recent Winners**  
  - 2025 – Italy (d. Spain 2-0)  
  - 2024 – Italy (d. Netherlands 2-0)  
  - 2023 – Italy (d. Australia 2-0)  
  - 2022 – Canada (d. Australia 2-0)  
  - 2021 – Russian Tennis Federation (d. Croatia 2-0)  
  - 2020 – *No final due to COVID‑19*  
  - 2019 – Spain (d. Canada 2‑0)  
- “The competition celebrated its **100th Final in 2012**.”  
- “The Finals format continued to evolve … with the Final 8 starting in Malaga in **2022**.”

- Covered entities: Davis Cup, United States, Great Britain, Australia, France, Sweden, Spain, Italy, Czechia/Germany/Russia, Croatia, Argentina, Canada, Serbia, South Africa, Switzerland, Netherlands.
